props.heading: Best trips from Guadalajara on a budget
props.subheading: Real flight, hotel, and activity costs for the destinations that actually fit what you have to spend — flying out of GDL.

props.text: Cabo San Lucas is actually the shortest flight from Guadalajara — shorter than the more famous Cancún — which surprises a lot of people planning the trip. Flying out of GDL, a trip to Oaxaca can start around $858 for flight, hotel, and activities together — not just the flight, pulled from our own cost data, not guesses.

features.title: Cancún — nonstop, ~2h40m–2h56m
features.text: Volaris and VivaAerobus fly it, about 5 times a day.

features.title: Oaxaca — nonstop, but thin (~11 flights/week)
features.text: Volaris is the only nonstop carrier, and it runs roughly every other day, not daily — check the schedule before locking in dates.

features.title: Cabo San Lucas — nonstop, ~1h35m–1h36m, the shortest of the three
features.text: VivaAerobus and Volaris fly it, roughly 4 times a day — genuinely quicker than the Cancún route despite Cancún being the more famous destination.

props.text: Los Cabos being the quickest flight of the three — shorter than Cancún — is a real, checkable surprise worth knowing before you book based on assumptions. Oaxaca's thin schedule, just one carrier flying every other day, signals it's booked as a deliberate cultural and culinary trip rather than an impulse weekend, which lines up with Guadalajara's own strong food and tequila culture pulling travelers toward Oaxaca's mezcal and mole scene.

items.question: Are these real-time prices?
items.answer: They're estimates based on our own curated cost data for this route and season, not a live quote — the real price on the partner site may be a bit higher or lower depending on exact dates.

items.question: Which destination has the shortest flight from Guadalajara?
items.answer: Cabo San Lucas, at about 1h35m nonstop — shorter than Cancún, which runs closer to 2h50m.

items.question: Is there a daily flight to Oaxaca from Guadalajara?
items.answer: Not quite — Volaris is the only nonstop carrier and it runs roughly every other day (about 11 flights a week), so check the schedule before locking in your dates.
